programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

Holed up in a hotel in a fictional European country, young Iris (Margaret Lockwood) befriends elderly Miss Froy (Dame May Whitty). When the train resumes, Iris suffers a bout of unconsciousness and wakes to find the old woman has disappeared. The other passengers ominously deny Miss Froy ever existed, so Iris begins to investigate with another traveller (Michael Redgrave) and, as the pair sleuth, romantic sparks fly.

Directed by Jonathan Demme and stars Tom Hanks (in his Oscar-winning role), Denzel Washington and Antonio Banderas.

programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

But ultimately, it shows the strength of love and hope to overcome shared traumas that Indigenous peoples from Australia, New Zealand and the South Pacific have continued to face.

When the train resumes, Iris suffers a bout of unconsciousness and wakes to find the old woman has disappeared. The other passengers ominously deny Miss Froy ever existed, so Iris begins to investigate with another traveller (Michael Redgrave) and, as the pair sleuth, romantic sparks fly.

programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.

programme.desc: Instagram claims more than a billion users on the planet, and more than 100 million photos posted every day. But what does this usage reveal about ourselves and our society? Instagram shapes our lives, it fills our brains with images that are supposed to bring us pleasure, to the point of overflowing, sometimes even depression. Young teenagers in search of recognition on the platform can get lost in this frantic quest for notoriety. Until they lose their sanity. Sometimes their life.

programme.sub-title: Ransomware Is Everywhere. Can It Be Stopped?
programme.desc: All over the world criminals are locking up important computer systems and demanding crypto as a ransom. So-called ransomware is officially an epidemic, and cryptocurrencies sit at the nexus of the crisis. In this episode of Cryptoland, we sift through the fallout of a ransomware attack at schools in Afton, Missouri, and our panellists discuss the history and current role of crypto in this booming type of cyber-crime.

programme.title: Cryptoland
programme.sub-title: How Bitcoin Mines Were Airlifted From China To The Us
programme.desc: The Chinese government has long tried to stamp out cryptocurrencies in the country with varying levels of success. In 2021, a ban on mining finally sent firms packing and seeking countries like Kazakhstan with friendlier stances toward crypto mining. They've also found homes in towns all over the US, where companies are encountering both support and criticism from locals, as well as politicians at the state and federal levels.
